paragraphs: LauraLynn is the only hospice for children in Ireland. A hospice cares for very sick people. It also helps their families. LauraLynn opened in 2001.
Now the Government will pay for all of its work. The Health Minister, Jennifer Carroll MacNeill, said this on Friday.
The State will give €11.5 million in 2027. LauraLynn workers will become public workers. LauraLynn will not need to collect money for medical care.
LauraLynn helps children there and at home. So fewer children need to stay in hospital for a long time. Its boss, Kerry McLaverty, is very happy. She says gifts from people will still help it grow.

國家將在2027年提供1150萬歐元。
LauraLynn的員工將成為公職人員。
安寧院將不需要再為醫療照顧募款。
LauraLynn在安寧院和家中幫助孩子。

paragraphs: The Government will pay the full cost of LauraLynn, the only children's hospice in Ireland. Health Minister Jennifer Carroll MacNeill made the announcement on Friday.

LauraLynn started in 2001. It cares for children who are very ill and supports their families. Children can stay at the hospice, or staff can help them in the community and at home. This means fewer children have to go into hospital, and others can go home from hospital sooner.

Under the new plan, LauraLynn will become a 'section 38' organisation. This means the HSE will make a formal agreement to fund its services, and its workers will become public servants. The State will give €11.5 million in 2027 to support the change.

Until now, the charity has depended on raising money to pay for medical care. That will no longer be needed. Chief executive Kerry McLaverty said the change gives the hospice a stronger future. She said it had taken many years and that donations will still help the service grow.
